newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says committed to missile sale to Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Russia says committed to missile sale to Cyprus.

text.p: Russia said on Monday it would go ahead with a controversial sale to the Greek Cypriot government of sophisticated anti-aircraft missile systems unless the divided island was declared a dimilitarised zone.
"The contracts have been signed and missiles will be shipped," Primakov told a news conference after talks in Moscow with Cypriot Foreign Minister Yiannakis Cassoulides.

"There will be no retreat," he added, referring to a strong pressure on Cyprus from the United States and Turkey to scrap the purchase of the S-300 missile system which Washington believes could upset the regional military balance.
Cyprus and Russia insist the missile complexes are a purely defensive system and reject complaints from the breakaway Turkish part of the island that they pose a military threat.
"No one can deny the need for Cyprus to have these defensive missile complexes," Cassoulides said.
Turkey, the only country to recognise breakaway northern Cyprus, has vowed to stop the deal by any means, including force.
Primakov appeared unconcerned by harsh statements by Turkey.
"There is a long way from verbal threats to their realisation and I urge you not to try and travel this distance even in your thoughts," he told reporters.
Primakov said that Russia placed high hopes on U.N.-led Cyprus peace talks due to start on July 9.

"Russia supports the idea of demilitarising Cyprus and sending an international peacekeeping force there," Primakov said. "Of course this should be a background for profound and active peace talks aimed at reaching a political solution."
